text:
Karthik: heads-up — node-pool-b showing steady KV cache growth during long-chat sessions, even after evictions kick in. +20% resident pages over 3 hours :thinking:
Nina: hmm do you have tenant breakdown? noisy neighbor suspects?
Karthik: yes, team-alpha and team-gamma smalls are churning a lot. but eviction logs show we keep freeing pages then reloading them almost immediately. looks like fragmentation + reuse mismatch.
Tomas: can you paste a short pprof cpu/mem snapshot?
Karthik: pasted below (trimmed):
```
# pprof heap - top
60.5%  kv_page_cache  45.2MB  hot: reuse_hotpath
20.0%  slab_fragments 15.0MB  small-allocs
# pprof cpu - top
40% evict_worker
25% page_reclaim
10% kernel_select
```
Nina: kernel_select at 10% stands out — are we falling back to slower kernels on these tenants due to sequence length/quantization mismatch?
Karthik: thats my hunch. longctx reqs pick a kernel path that increases page churn because it touches more KV entries per token. combine that with small-tenant quotas -> they never build good residency, keep getting evicted.
perf-bot: ALERT: kv-residency-growth - node-pool-b - threshold breached (3h, +18% resident pages). Logged incident ID: INC-20260315-42
Ops: adding increased OOM guard for the pool, but we should fix root cause. what are mitigations?
Nina: options: 1) per-tenant aging windows (decay hotness slower for small active tenants), 2) quota-smoothing (allow short burst residency for tenants hitting reuse), 3) change kernel-selection heuristic to prefer reuse-friendly kernel when longctx detection and high page-fault rate combine.
Tomas: can we simulate kernel-switch heuristics cheaply? maybe a runtime flag to force the alternative kernel on a subset of tenant traffic and measure page-fault/sec and evict rate.
Karthik: I ran a mini A/B yesterday. forcing reuse-friendly kernel on 10% of team-alpha traffic dropped page_faults/sec from ~240 to ~60 and reduced eviction churn by ~3x. cpu cost rose ~6% but overall p99 latency unchanged.
Ops: that sounds promising. what's the config change?
Karthik: runtime flag: `kv_kernel_preference=reuse_friendly` scoped to tenant. I can roll a canary to 5% then 25%. need signoff for the rollout plan + metrics to watch: page_faults/sec, evicts/min, resident_pages, p99 latency.
Nina: also add a fallback: if resident_pages > X and evicts/min > Y, temporarily tighten quotas to stop collateral damage.
Tomas: agree. I'll wire an experiment in staging to test kernel flag + quota smoothing. can we get perf-bot to annotate the experiment results automatically?
perf-bot: noted. will tag experiment metrics and post summary when complete. use label `kv-kernel-expt-20260315`
Karthik: timeline: canary today 5% for team-alpha, collect 2h of data, escalate to 25% if metrics look good. I'll prepare the rollout doc in #eng-releases (short runbook).
Ops: I'll monitor node-pool-b and stand by to revert if memory growth resumes. :thumbsup:
Nina: one more ask — add a quick probe to the eviction path to log when a page is evicted and re-requested within 10s (easy grep). that'll help quantify reuse-after-evict.
Karthik: will do. logging snippet I'll add:
```
EVICT: tenant=%s page=%d ts=%s
RELOAD: tenant=%s page=%d ts=%s delta_s=%d
```
Tomas: perfect. thanks all — let's reconvene after the canary window.
